messages.author: c30c9e29d10d3cd7
messages.subject: Raster predictions adjusted for area
parts:
I am interested in accounting for sampling area in my models.
In chapter 8.3, pg 439 of the "Applied hierarchical modelling in ecology book" offset(log(area)) is used in the model equations. Why is it log of area?

Also when do you use density in the model and when do you use abundance?

Thanks,

I

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Raster predictions adjusted for area
parts:
log(area) is used because abundance is modeled on the log scale. i.e., log(lambda) = stuff.  Under the Poisson model we expect that lambda scales with area:  lambda(A) = A*lambda0.  Therefore log(A) should appear as an additive effect.

Whether you use density or abundance is purely a matter of preference.

regards
andy

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] Raster predictions adjusted for area
parts:
hi Ian,

because in a Poisson regression you have this for the counts C:

C ~ Poisson(A * lambda)

where the expected count (inside the parentheses) is the product of an "area" and a per-area-unit density called lambda. Then, when you model pattern in the expected count, you get this:

log(A) + log(stuff)

A is called an offset and it's the natural log of whatever measure of sampling effort (time or space) you have. lambda then gets the interpretation if a "density" per 1 unit in which effort is expressed.

Best regards  --- Marc


PS: See page 105 in the AHM1 book
